intent: One hospital on the lake: the date, the failed first dose and the blood-sugar counter dropping, the dogs and the borrowed lab, then the DEATH SENTENCE plate wiped away for a dollar.
pacing_profile: question read verbatim, three options, 3-s beat, reveal with the number, story beats shaped per episode (brief.md), punchline + short follow
pause_policy: Pause only at the marked ellipses; the beat is real silence (ticks come from quizscore.py).
title: In which city was insulin FIRST injected into a patient?

lines.direction: the question, cold — curiosity comes from the map moving under it
lines.text: In which city was insulin first injected into a patient?

lines.direction: quick, each option its own beat

lines.text: Toronto. On 11 January 1922, at Toronto General Hospital, 14-year-old Leonard Thompson got the first injection.

lines.direction: tighten on the lakeshore; a vial sticker on 'impure'; on 'later' the blood-sugar counter runs down from 0.52 to 0.12 like the 1922 case notes; a green check on 'normal' and the Canadian flag-ball grins
lines.text: The first dose was impure. 12 days later a purified extract dropped his blood sugar to normal.

lines.direction: ease back to the university; a microscope sticker on 'Banting'; the PROBLEM / ANSWER split (1889 Minkowski, 1921 Toronto) on 'dog' with a dog sticker in the right column; the split folds and the SUMMER 1921 card and the lab tag land on 'lab'; Canada pulses
lines.text: Banting and Best had extracted it from dog pancreases the summer before, in a borrowed university lab.

lines.direction: pull back over Ontario; the FATAL plate waits at the bottom; a scroll sticker on 'patent'; the $1 card on 'dollar' and the British flag-ball thinks; on 'sentence' the plate wipes away and Canada pulses
lines.text: Banting sold the patent to the university for a single dollar. Diabetes stopped being a death sentence.

lines.direction: punchline, then a short follow — the outro visual asks
lines.text: A dollar well spent. Follow us.
